faqs.question: Is it legal to jam drones on my property?
faqs.answer: In most countries, including the US, signal jamming devices are illegal for civilian use as they can interfere with authorized communications. Only law enforcement and military typically have permission to use drone jammers. Always check local laws before purchasing countermeasure devices.

faqs.question: How can I tell if a drone is spying on me?
faqs.answer: Look for drones hovering near your property, especially around windows or private areas. Listen for buzzing sounds and watch for unusual flight patterns. RF detectors and drone detection apps can help identify nearby drones, though they have limitations in range and accuracy.

faqs.question: What should I do if I spot a spy drone?
faqs.answer: Document the incident with photos or video, note the time and location, and report it to local authorities if you suspect illegal surveillance. Avoid attempting to physically intercept the drone, as this may be illegal. Focus on passive detection and legal reporting channels.

faqs.question: Can drone surveillance see inside my home?
faqs.answer: Standard consumer drones cannot see through walls, but they can observe through windows and monitor outdoor activities. Thermal imaging drones can detect heat signatures through some materials. Use privacy screens, close blinds, and limit sensitive outdoor activities when drone activity is suspected.

faqs.question: Are there privacy laws protecting against drone surveillance?
faqs.answer: Privacy laws vary by jurisdiction, but many countries have regulations restricting drone flights over private property and requiring pilot identification. The EU's GDPR and various national privacy acts may apply to drone surveillance. Research local drone laws and privacy regulations in your area for specific protections.
